To start the MongoDB instance with authentication and specify the data directory path using `mongod`, you would use the following command:

- **--dbpath /data/**: Specifies the path where the database files will be stored.

After running this command, MongoDB will initialize its configuration and start the process without requiring any additional user input. It will automatically prompt you when it needs to authenticate users during startup or when connecting to the server via the shell or administrative APIs.

If you want to manually connect to the running MongoDB instance after starting it, you can do so from another terminal window using the connection string provided by the server (e.g., `localhost:27017`). If authentication is enabled, you'll need to provide your credentials when prompted in the shell.

Note that if you encounter an error related to "No suitable driver" when trying to connect, make sure you have installed the appropriate MongoDB driver for your environment (e.g., `mongo` on Linux/macOS or `MongoDB.Driver` on Windows).
